issues.legal_issue: A person challenging a determination that property is a waqf may qualify as a person interested in the waqf even while denying that the property is a waqf.
material_facts: The plaintiffs challenged a notification treating the shrine properties as a waqf and claimed an interest in those properties as members of their managing committee.
The plaintiffs denied that the properties were subject to the governing waqf regime; their pleadings also described the waqf as falling within an exemption from that regime.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs were persons interested in the transaction held to be a waqf, so their suit fell within the class of suits governed by the special limitation provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5(2) of the United Provinces Muslims Waqfs Act, 1936, “any person interested in a waqf” includes a person interested in a transaction held by the Commissioner of Waqfs to be a waqf. A literal construction that would make the provision allowing a challenge to that determination ineffective must give way to a liberal construction that makes the whole provision effective. The Court relied on Chaturbhuj Mohanlal v. Bhicam Chand Chororia & Sons, Mathu Kutty v. Varoe Kutty, and Lal Chand v. Messrs. Basanta Mal Devi Dayal & Ors.; it also used the construction of “any party to an arbitration agreement” in section 33 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, as an analogy.

predicates.waqf_determination_challenge_suit: The plaintiffs brought a suit challenging an official determination that property was a waqf.
predicates.plaintiffs_claim_interest_in_disputed_pr: The plaintiffs claimed a proprietary, management, or other interest in the disputed property.
predicates.property_was_determined_to_be_waqf: An official determination treated the disputed property as a waqf.

issues.definition: When a suit challenges a determination that property is a waqf and its plaintiffs claim an interest in that property, they count as interested in the alleged waqf.

issues.legal_issue: Time is excluded from limitation only when an order or injunction stays the institution of the suit, and an order directing a committee not to interfere with an institution’s affairs does not suffice if it does not bar the suit.
material_facts: An earlier suit resulted in an order removing the plaintiffs from a managing committee and directing them not to interfere with the institution’s affairs as committee members.
The order did not expressly or by necessary implication prohibit the plaintiffs from filing the later suit.
The later suit arose from a notification and subsequent steps taken after the earlier order, and it was filed beyond the applicable limitation period measured from the notification.
issues.conclusion: The earlier order did not trigger exclusion of time under section 15 of the Limitation Act, 1908, and the suit was barred by limitation under section 5(2) of the waqf statute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15 of the Limitation Act, 1908, excludes time only where the institution of the suit has been stayed by an injunction or order; the test is whether filing the suit would violate the order. Limitation provisions are applied according to their strict grammatical meaning, without equitable enlargement. The Court relied on Nagendra Nath Dey v. Suresh Chandra Dey, Narayan Jivangouda v. Puttabai, Beti Maharani v. The Collector of Etawah, and Sundaramma v. Abdul Khader, and held Musammat Basso Kaur v. Lala Dhua Singh inapplicable.

rule.if: suit_challenges_waqf_determination and prior_order_existed and prior_order_did_not_stay_suit_filing and suit_was_filed_outside_applicable_limitation_window

predicates.suit_challenges_waqf_determination: The proceeding is a suit challenging an official determination that property is a waqf.
predicates.prior_order_existed: A court made an order in an earlier proceeding involving the plaintiffs.
predicates.prior_order_did_not_stay_suit_filing: The earlier order did not expressly or by necessary implication prohibit institution of the later suit.
predicates.suit_was_filed_outside_applicable_limita: The later suit was filed after the applicable limitation window had expired, unless time was excluded.

issues.definition: If a waqf-determination challenge is filed outside its limitation window and an earlier court order did not stay its filing, time spent in the earlier proceeding is not excluded and the suit is time barred.

issues.legal_issue: A suit against a waqf board concerning its purported acts or seeking relief in respect of a waqf requires prior statutory notice, even if recurring offerings to a notified shrine were not separately listed in the notification.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sued the central board over its assumption of authority and management steps concerning the shrine and its properties.
The notification identified the shrine as the waqf, but did not separately list offerings made by devotees.
The offerings were made from time to time and formed income of the shrine.
The plaintiffs did not give the board the required notice before filing suit.
issues.conclusion: The omission of recurring offerings from the notification did not take them outside the waqf or make the notification defective; the notice requirement applied, and the suit was not maintainable because notice had not been given.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53 of the United Provinces Muslims Waqfs Act, 1936, applies both to suits concerning acts purportedly done by a Central Board under the Act and to suits seeking relief in respect of a waqf; the Court noted its similarity to section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Offerings made from time to time by devotees are, by their nature, income of the shrine and need not be separately specified in the notification.

rule.if: suit_is_against_board_for_purported_waqf_act_or_seeks_relief_concerning_waqf and notification_identified_shrine_as_waqf and recurring_offerings_were_shrine_income and required_notice_was_not_given

predicates.suit_is_against_board_for_purported_waqf: The proceeding is a suit against a waqf board concerning an act it purported to take, or seeking relief concerning a waqf.
predicates.notification_identified_shrine_as_waqf: The notification identified the shrine as property treated as a waqf.
predicates.recurring_offerings_were_shrine_income: Devotees made offerings from time to time, and those offerings formed income of the shrine.
predicates.required_notice_was_not_given: The plaintiff filed the suit without first giving the required notice to the board.

issues.definition: A suit concerning a board’s purported waqf-related act or seeking relief concerning a waqf is not maintainable when the shrine was identified as a waqf, its recurring offerings were income, and the required notice was not given.
